entities.name: FingerVision
entities.desc: Japan's leading tactile sensor startup for robotics. **Vision-based tactile sensing:** FingerVision's approach uses a small camera inside a transparent elastomer fingertip; AI processes the deformation images to infer force, slip, and texture — enabling dexterous manipulation without conventional strain-gauge sensors that are expensive and fragile. The approach is both lower-cost and more data-rich than traditional force-torque sensors. **Market:** Tier-1 robotics OEMs (Japanese and international humanoid makers) and food-handling automation — food manipulation requires particularly sophisticated soft-grasp capability. FingerVision is part of Japan's emerging robotics component ecosystem that positions Japan as a supplier into the global humanoid supply chain, alongside precision actuator, harmonic drive, and sensor companies.

tags.l: Scarce ingredient: touch data for physical AI

entities.bio: Founded 2022, Tokyo, by Yuki Nono (CEO) — former researcher at Carnegie Mellon University and Tohoku University. Private; backed by Japanese VCs. Core product: vision-based tactile fingertip sensors that give robots a sense of touch via embedded cameras and AI, rather than traditional strain-gauge sensors.

entities.name: SB Neo
entities.desc: SoftBank's newest AI entity — a neocloud play targeting the US enterprise AI market launched just days before this landscape was updated. SB Neo's thesis: Japanese-owned, US-sited AI cloud infrastructure gives enterprises an alternative to the US Big Three hyperscalers (AWS, Azure, GCP) that is less subject to US government political pressure, while also being more sovereign than Chinese-backed alternatives. SoftBank's Vision Fund portfolio of 400+ companies provides a natural enterprise customer base for SB Neo services. The neocloud category (CoreWeave, Lambda Labs, Oracle Cloud AI) is crowded; SB Neo's differentiation will depend on Arm chip integration (SoftBank's ARM stake) and SoftBank's ability to pre-commit Vision Fund portfolio companies as anchor tenants.
entities.bio: Founded July 2026, as a joint venture between SoftBank Corp (51%) and SoftBank Group (49%). Operates as a US-targeted neocloud company, positioning itself as a Japanese-backed alternative AI cloud platform for enterprise workloads in North America. No public CEO appointment as of August 2026.

entities.name: Micron Hiroshima
entities.desc: The only US DRAM manufacturing presence in Asia — a strategic anchor in the US-Japan semiconductor alliance. Micron's Hiroshima facility is one of two locations (with Taichung, Taiwan) producing HBM2e and HBM3e memory stacks for Nvidia, AMD, and Intel AI accelerators. **HBM supercycle:** Each new generation of AI training chip (Nvidia H100→H200→B200) uses 2–4x more HBM than its predecessor; Micron Hiroshima is capacity-constrained into 2026. **CHIPS Act adjacency:** Micron is simultaneously building a $100B US HBM fab (New York State) with US CHIPS Act subsidy, but Hiroshima remains critical for near-term HBM supply. The Elpida acquisition (2013, from bankruptcy) was Micron's entry into Japan's DRAM industry — an inflection point that made Hiroshima the de facto US memory manufacturing outpost in Japan.
entities.bio: Micron Technology's Japan manufacturing subsidiary, located in Higashihiroshima. Micron Technology (founded 1978, Boise ID, NASDAQ: MU) is the only remaining US-owned DRAM and NAND manufacturer. The Hiroshima facility has produced DRAM since 1980 (acquired from Elpida Memory, 2013) and now produces HBM (High Bandwidth Memory) for AI accelerators.

entities.name: Tower Semiconductor Japan
entities.zh: タワーセミコンダクター日本
entities.desc: Specialty analog and RF semiconductor foundry, relevant in this landscape for its Japan manufacturing footprint in a geopolitically important category. Tower's Agrate (Italy), Newport Beach (US), and Nishiwaki (Japan) fabs produce analog chips for imaging sensors, automotive ADAS radar, and power management — critical inputs for AI vision systems and autonomous vehicle radars. Japan's analog chip supply chain is a quiet strategic asset: Japanese firms (Shin-Etsu, SUMCO for wafers; Tower, Renesas for fab) form a nearly complete analog supply chain that supplements the TSMC-centered digital logic chain.
entities.bio: Tower Semiconductor's Japan subsidiary, operating fabs previously acquired from Panasonic. Tower Semiconductor (founded 1993, Migdal HaEmek, Israel; listed NASDAQ TSEM) is a specialty foundry for analog, RF, and mixed-signal chips. Intel attempted to acquire Tower for $5.4B (2022) but abandoned the deal in 2023.

entities.name: Hitachi
entities.desc: **Fanuc physical AI partnership (#127, Sept 30, 2026):** strategic partnership with Fanuc to commercialize physical AI for factories. Hitachi supplies HMAX Industry AI, its own edge AI chips and digital twin simulation; Fanuc supplies AI-capable robots and controllers. Proof of concept runs at Hitachi's Ibaraki plants as 'customer zero' on parts picking and line changeovers through FY2027, then joint global sales across semiconductors, pharma, autos, logistics, food, shipbuilding and agriculture. No financial terms. It is Hitachi's second robot-maker deal in a week, after Agile Robots. **Agile Robots physical AI partnership (#123, Sept 29, 2026):** basic agreement with Munich-based Agile Robots (DLR spin-out, 2018; ~3,500 staff; 20,000+ robot installations; SoftBank Vision Fund 2 led its 2021 Series C) to co-develop the 'brain' for industrial robots, combining Hitachi's tacit-knowledge learning model and in-house low-power edge AI chip for vision and tactile data with Agile's AgileCore platform, arms, mobile robots and Agile ONE humanoid. Resulting models will be sold globally inside HMAX Industry via the Connective Industries sector; no financial terms or timeline disclosed. Japan's largest industrial conglomerate, executing a focused AI transformation under CEO Kojima's 'Social Innovation Business' strategy. **Lumada:** Hitachi's AI and digital twin platform for industrial customers — deployed in railways (predictive track maintenance), manufacturing (AI quality inspection), and energy (grid optimization). Lumada revenue exceeded ¥1T ($6.7B) in FY2024, growing faster than the group average. **GlobalLogic integration:** The $9.6B GlobalLogic acquisition (2021) gives Hitachi 25,000+ software engineers — dramatically expanding its software-first AI delivery capability beyond traditional hardware. **Hitachi Energy:** AI-driven grid management tools for energy transition infrastructure — a structural growth market as data centers (and humanoid robot charging networks) increase power grid demand. **Hitachi High-Tech x Powrex physical AI battery coating (Aug 20, 2026):** Hitachi High-Tech completed a demonstration with Powrex applying its HMAX Industry physical AI (PROACCELA process informatics + XRF/SEM analysis) to optimize cathode-coating conditions for all-solid-state batteries — a step toward commercializing a Lab-to-Fab process aimed at cutting the specialized-engineer bottleneck in battery scale-up ahead of the market's expected takeoff around 2030. **Bloom Energy partnership: on-site fuel cells for AI data-center power (#96, Sept 1-2, 2026):** Hitachi and Bloom Energy announced a partnership to deploy on-site solid-oxide fuel cell power systems at Japanese data centers and industrial facilities, targeting the grid-connection delays and rising electricity demand that AI infrastructure buildout is creating. Hitachi leads planning, design, development, and operational support; Bloom Energy supplies the fuel cell systems, which can run on natural gas, biogas, or hydrogen and generate power directly on-site rather than waiting on constrained grid capacity. A pilot at Hitachi's own Omika Works demonstrated remote power control and multi-unit efficiency at scale, integrating Bloom's cells with Hitachi's control systems. The deal is a power-infrastructure play adjacent to Hitachi's existing Hitachi Energy grid business — positioning Hitachi to capture data-center and fab construction spending (Rapidus, TSMC JASM, Kioxia) that is increasingly bottlenecked by grid connection timelines rather than chip supply itself. **HMAX expanded with Data Center, Cyber, Data Fabric, AI Operations modules (#107, Sept 3, 2026):** Hitachi unveiled an expansion of its HMAX physical-AI suite at the Hitachi Social Innovation Forum 2026 Japan (Sept 3-4, Tokyo), adding HMAX Data Center -- a one-stop suite for autonomous monitoring and optimization of power, IT, and cooling infrastructure at data centers -- alongside three cross-domain foundry solutions: HMAX Cyber (an Identify/Manage/Recover operational-resilience service), HMAX Data Fabric (an ontology-based knowledge graph that converts field data and veteran-operator tacit knowledge into AI-usable form), and HMAX AI Operations. The launch leans on Hitachi's combined IT/OT/product expertise and its Physical AI Forward Deployed Engineer teams, and is explicitly framed around Japan's social-infrastructure labor shortage -- fewer skilled personnel available to maintain increasingly complex facilities. Positioned against the AI data-center capex buildout (NTT, Blackstone, Microsoft, Itochu all expanding Japan capacity through 2033), HMAX Data Center gives Hitachi a monetization angle on the operations-and-maintenance side of that buildout rather than the construction side -- a distinct, higher-margin layer of the same infrastructure cycle.

entities.bio: Founded 1910, Ibaraki Prefecture, by Namihei Odaira. President & CEO: Toshiaki Tokunaga (since April 2025). Listed TSE (6501). Japan's most diversified industrial conglomerate; key subsidiaries include Hitachi Vantara (data/storage), Hitachi Energy (power infrastructure), Hitachi Astemo (automotive systems), and GlobalLogic (US IT consulting, acquired 2021 for $9.6B). Revenue FY2024 ~¥10T ($67B).

entities.name: Toshiba
entities.desc: **Power-chip merger talks stall (#130, Sept 30-Oct 2, 2026):** Toshiba's Device & Storage unit (silicon MOSFETs) is one of three parties, with Rohm and Mitsubishi Electric, to the March 27 basic agreement to integrate power-semiconductor businesses; talks missed their summer target over equity ratios and leadership, with November the new goal. Toshiba and Rohm already share power-device production under a 2023 METI-subsidized tie-up. Japan's most significant corporate governance failure of the 21st century — now a private company working to rebuild post-privatization (Oct 2023). Toshiba sold its NAND flash memory business (now Kioxia) in 2018 following nuclear-subsidiary (Westinghouse) losses; sold Toshiba Medical to Canon (2016); sold its consumer electronics brand to various buyers. **Remaining assets:** Industrial infrastructure (nuclear, water, rail), Toshiba Tec, and a ~40% stake in Kioxia. Post-privatization JIP's mandate is to restructure and eventually relist. Toshiba's trajectory is cautionary context for Japanese corporate AI transformation: a company that led in semiconductors, nuclear, and consumer electronics and failed to manage the transition to software-first competition.

tags.l: Power-chip merger talks with Rohm/Mitsubishi Electric

entities.bio: Founded 1939 (merger of Tokyo Shibaura Electric and others), Kawasaki. Privatized October 2023 by Japan Industrial Partners (JIP) consortium after years of financial scandals and governance crises. Former CEO: Taro Shimada (post-privatization). Principal subsidiaries: Toshiba Tec (POS systems), Toshiba Infrastructure Systems, and minority stakes in Kioxia (NAND flash).

entities.name: Disco
entities.desc: A monopoly position in a critical but invisible step: slicing completed semiconductor wafers into individual chips (dicing). Every AI chip in this landscape — Nvidia H100, Huawei Ascend, CXMT DRAM — is cut from a silicon wafer using a Disco dicing saw. **AI demand flywheel:** More chips → more dicing required → more Disco equipment sold. Disco also makes wafer thinning grinders critical for 3D chip stacking (CoWoS, SoIC), which is the packaging technology that enables HBM3 and next-generation 3D AI chips. Disco's ~80% global market share in dicing means it has near-monopoly leverage over the timing of new chip production ramps. The company's unique internal economy ('Will' allocation system — all internal transactions priced at market rates) is a widely cited management case study. **Caught in the Sept 14-15 AI-safety selloff (#108):** Shares declined more than 1% Tuesday alongside Lasertec as the broader chip-equipment complex sold off on Anthropic/OpenAI AI-safety warnings (see Tokyo Electron, Advantest) — a sentiment-driven move rather than any change to Disco's own order book or the record Apr-Jun shipment figures below.
entities.bio: Founded 1937, Ota City, Tokyo. CEO: Kazuma Sekiya. Listed TSE (6146). World's dominant maker of dicing saws, grinders, and laser cutters for semiconductor wafer slicing and thinning. ~80% global market share in dicing saws. Revenue FY2024 ~¥320B ($2.1B).

entities.name: GPIF
entities.zh: 年金積立金管理運用独立行政法人
entities.py: Nenkin Tsumitatekin Kanri Un'yō Dokuritsu Gyōsei Hōjin
entities.desc: The world's largest pension fund — GPIF's portfolio decisions are among the most consequential in global capital markets. As of mid-2026, GPIF holds ~25% in domestic equities (TSE Prime), 25% in international equities, 25% in domestic bonds, and 25% in international bonds. **AI exposure:** GPIF's domestic equity portfolio includes every major Japanese company in this landscape (Hitachi, Fanuc, TEL, Shin-Etsu, Renesas). Its international equity portfolio includes Nvidia, Microsoft, Apple — the primary AI infrastructure companies. **Passive vs. active:** GPIF runs mostly passive indexed strategies, meaning AI sector outperformance directly boosts GPIF returns but GPIF cannot dynamically overweight AI. ESG investing standards have been a controversial constraint on certain defense-adjacent holdings. **Santander: up to $62bn of Treasuries sellable without a formal policy change (#108, Sept 8-11, 2026):** An unusually convened management-committee meeting on Aug 21 — GPIF's first publicly announced August meeting in seven years — fueled speculation the $2 trillion fund is reconsidering its tilt toward foreign bonds. Health Minister Kenichiro Ueno said Sept 8 that GPIF decided in March a formal review wasn't needed but is 'continuing to consider the matter in an appropriate way.' Santander analysts estimated Sept 11 that GPIF could sell as much as $62bn of US Treasuries purely by trimming foreign bonds to 20% from current levels — still within its existing 25%±5pp band — alongside a technical tweak to how it tracks the FTSE World Government Bond Index; domestic bonds already reached 27% of the portfolio by end-March, above the 25% benchmark, giving room to lean further into JGBs without any headline policy change. The debate sits against a 10-year JGB yield that touched 3% for the first time since 1996 the same week — for global fixed-income investors, a multi-percentage-point shift by the world's largest pension allocator would be one of the more consequential rebalancing events of the year, a potential incremental drag on Treasuries and backstop bid for JGBs, even though nothing has been formally decided.

entities.bio: Government Pension Investment Fund (GPIF, 年金積立金管理運用独立行政法人), Tokyo. The world's largest pension fund with ~¥250T ($1.7T) in AUM. President: Masataka Miyazono. Invests in domestic and international equities, bonds, and alternative assets on behalf of Japan's public pension system.

entities.name: JPYC
entities.desc: Japan's first legally compliant JPY stablecoin — issued under Japan's Fund Settlement Act, which requires stablecoin issuers to be licensed financial institutions. **AZ-COM Maruwa payroll pilot:** JPYC partnered with AZ-COM Maruwa (a major Amazon Japan logistics company) to pilot paying delivery drivers in JPYC — the first stablecoin payroll implementation in Japan, testing Japanese regulators' appetite for crypto-native payroll infrastructure. **Regulatory readiness:** Japan's Payment Services Act amendment (2023) created one of the world's clearest legal frameworks for stablecoin issuance; JPYC is positioned as the most compliance-ready JPY stablecoin for the opening of institutional digital asset markets in Japan in 2025–2026. Circle (USDC) as investor signals international stablecoin infrastructure convergence. **¥1,000,000 transaction cap lifted (confirmed Aug 24, 2026):** The FSA removed the per-transaction ceiling that had confined second-category Funds Transfer Service Providers like JPYC to retail micropayments since 2023, paired with the FSA's new dedicated Crypto/Stablecoin Division to supervise the larger flows now permitted. JPYC can now structurally compete for B2B settlement and treasury business, though trust-bank-backed JPYSC (SBI Shinsei Trust Bank) retains a stronger legal claim to reserves under trust law.
entities.bio: Founded 2021, Tokyo, by Noritaka Okabe (岡部典孝, CEO). Private; backed by Circle (USDC issuer), SBI Holdings, and others. Japan's first and only legally compliant JPY-pegged stablecoin (under Japan's Fund Settlement Act). JPYC Inc. is the issuer.

entities.name: AZ-COM Maruwa
entities.zh: AZ-COM丸和ホールディングス
entities.desc: Japan's largest independent Amazon delivery partner — roughly 20% of Amazon Japan's last-mile delivery volume passes through Maruwa's network. **JPYC payroll pilot:** Partnered with JPYC to pilot driver compensation in JPY stablecoins — Japan's first stablecoin payroll implementation, addressing the endemic driver wage underpayment problem in Japan's trucking sector. **2024 Logistics Law Reform:** Japan's mandatory 'Truck Driver Working Hours' legislation (April 2024) — the so-called '2024 logistics problem' — capped truck driver overtime and created acute capacity shortages; Maruwa's scale and Amazon relationship give it pricing power to offset higher labor costs but also pressure to adopt automation faster than smaller peers. AZ-COM Maruwa's interest in JPYC is as much about reducing payroll processing friction as it is about crypto adoption.
entities.bio: Founded 1970, Maruwa District (Nagano Prefecture), by Masaru Wasami (和澄賢, founder and current president). Private. Japan's largest independent logistics company not affiliated with a major telecom or trading house; principal customer is Amazon Japan, for which Maruwa operates a significant portion of last-mile delivery in Japan.

entities.name: Advantest
entities.desc: World leader in semiconductor automated test equipment (ATE), with dominant share in testers for AI accelerators and HBM — making it one of the highest-beta AI names on the Tokyo exchange. Fell sharply in the July 24, 2026 AI-valuation rout alongside Tokyo Electron and Kioxia. Reports earnings the week of July 28 alongside SCREEN Holdings and Tokyo Electron, into a Nikkei that has lost more than 7% in July and slid into correction — making its order commentary a key read on whether AI-test demand is actually softening or just being repriced. **Q1 FY2026 results, first of the equipment gauntlet (#60, Jul 29 2026):** Reported record Q1 profit — EPS $1.51, net margin 33.2%, ROE 55.98% — on strong demand, favorable product mix and FX gains across CPU, GPU, custom-ASIC and networking testers. Management raised its view of the SoC tester market and said capacity expansion is being pulled forward. Shares still fell 1.22% to ¥25,200, as investors focused on a cautious margin outlook rather than the record top line — the first print in the Advantest (Jul 29) → Tokyo Electron (Jul 30) → Kioxia (Jul 31) equipment/memory earnings sequence that follows the July 28 CXMT-triggered sell-off. **FY2026 guidance raised 35% (#62, Jul 29-31 2026):** Follow-through from the Q1 print: management lifted full-year operating-profit guidance to ¥846.0bn on ¥1.714tn revenue — implying roughly 70% YoY growth, up from a prior forecast of about 26%, and above the ~42% consensus had modeled — after AI-inference tester demand outran what the company assumed as recently as April. Advantest also raised its view of the global semiconductor tester market to $13.0–14.5bn for the year, a record and about 19% above its April forecast. Shares jumped as much as 10.9% intraday on the update, part of a broader Nikkei rally (+4.0% Jul 31) that also lifted Tokyo Electron and Kioxia — a reversal from the cautious Jul 29 reaction and a reminder that the stock is trading on forward order-book signals as much as trailing results. **Nvidia-beat rally fades intraday (#90, Aug 27, 2026):** Rose in early Tokyo trade after Nvidia's blowout Q2 report before reversing to close down 1.96% as the broader Nikkei chip-stock rally faded into profit-taking — another data point that Advantest's high AI-beta cuts both ways within a single session, not just over weeks. **AI-safety selloff: -4.5% then -2%+ over two sessions (#108, Sept 14-15, 2026):** Advantest fell 4.5% Monday and more than 2% further Tuesday as Anthropic/OpenAI AI-safety warnings triggered a broad de-rating of AI-linked names (see SoftBank, Tokyo Electron), with Kioxia (-8.6% Monday) leading the memory/equipment complex lower. The size of the move relative to Tokyo Electron's underscores Advantest's position as the highest-beta name in the group — its tester franchise is levered almost entirely to AI-accelerator and HBM volumes, with no diversified equipment base to cushion sentiment swings.

tags.l: Early rally on Nvidia beat, closed -1.96% (Aug 27)

entities.bio: Founded 1954, Tokyo. CEO: Yoshiaki Yoshida. Listed TSE (6857) and NYSE (ATE). World's largest semiconductor test equipment maker (~50% global market share in SoC and DRAM testers). Revenue FY2024 ¥330B (.2B). Critical infrastructure vendor: every AI chip (Nvidia H100, Huawei Ascend, CXMT DRAM) must pass Advantest testers before shipment.

entities.name: Sierra
entities.desc: US enterprise AI agent platform expanding to Japan through SoftBank's distribution partnership. Sierra's core product replaces traditional IVR and chatbot systems with AI agents that can handle end-to-end customer service conversations with context and decision-making autonomy. **Japan market strategy:** SoftBank's exclusive distribution partnership gives Sierra immediate access to SoftBank's enterprise client base (Japan's largest telecom with 200M+ service interactions/year) without needing to build a Japan sales team from scratch. **Competitive position:** Competes with Salesforce Agentforce, Oracle, and Japanese domestic vendors (PKSHA, Fujitsu) in the Japanese enterprise AI agent market. Sierra is relevant to this landscape because the SoftBank partnership pattern (US AI startup + SoftBank exclusive Japan distribution) has become a repeating template in Japan's AI market after the OpenAI (SB OAI Japan) precedent.

Private; raised $1.58B from Sequoia Capital and Benchmark Capital. SoftBank is Sierra's exclusive Japan distribution partner. Core product: AI agent platform for enterprise customer service.

entities.name: Cabinet Office (CEFP)
entities.zh: 内閣府・経済財政諮問会議
entities.desc: **Year-end AI action plan ordered (#125, Oct 1, 2026):** At the Japan Growth Strategy Council (日本成長戦略会議), Takaichi ordered a 行動計画 by year-end to spread high-performance AI (高性能AI) through the economy, including industrial-structure change, and the council fixed FY2027-FY2031 as the concentrated investment period (集中投資期間) for the 17 strategic sectors. AI and semiconductors account for ¥101.6tn of the ¥370tn+ public-private roadmap to FY2040, which targets ~¥250tn annual private capex and ~¥1,100tn nominal GDP; member Matsuo Yutaka proposed a fully domestic chip-to-robot supply chain packaged for export. The growth strategy execution plan and FY2027 budget are due on the same December timetable. Drafting body for the annual Basic Policy on Economic and Fiscal Management and Reform (骨太の方針). The Takaichi cabinet approved its first edition July 21, 2026: 'responsible and proactive fiscal policy,' ~¥370tn in public-private investment into strategic sectors including AI and semiconductors through FY2040, targets of >1% real and >3% nominal growth, and — notably — removal of the phrase 'fiscal consolidation' in favor of a stable-reduction anchor on the debt-to-GDP ratio. Bond market response was wary, with the long-term rate near 30-year highs and BOJ-independence questions unresolved ahead of the July 30 MPM. **Approval rating slide (#58, Jul 26-27 2026):** A Yomiuri poll fielded Jul 24-26 showed cabinet approval falling to 57% from 69% in June — the first sub-60% reading since Takaichi took office — with disapproval of cost-of-living policy rising to 71% from 56%. The government has delayed its pledged cut to the 8% food consumption-tax rate amid intra-LDP resistance and bond-market sensitivity, leaving the honebuto's ¥370tn growth pledge harder to square with near-term household relief. **FY2026 GDP forecast cut as Korea, Taiwan overtake Japan in exports (#70, Aug 7, 2026):** A Nikkei Asia analysis showed South Korea ($496.3bn) and Taiwan ($416.6bn) each surpassed Japan ($384.4bn) in total H1 2026 exports for the first time, as AI-chip demand drove South Korean semiconductor exports (including SSDs) up 162.6% YoY to $192.4bn — already exceeding all of 2025. Japan's exposure is concentrated in semiconductor materials and manufacturing equipment (Tokyo Electron, Shin-Etsu, SUMCO) rather than the AI logic/memory chips themselves (Samsung, SK Hynix, TSMC) capturing the demand surge. The Cabinet Office response: its FY2026 real GDP growth forecast was cut to 0.9% from an earlier 1.3%, even as South Korea raised its own 2026 growth forecast from 2.0% to 3.0% — a direct trade-competitiveness read-through for the honebuto's ¥370tn strategic-investment pledge, and a reminder that Noetra/Rapidus's payoff is still years from showing up in the export data. **Preliminary Q2 GDP due (Aug 17, 2026):** The Economic and Social Research Institute's first preliminary April-June GDP estimate — the reference data point for both the honebuto's ¥370tn growth pledge and the BOJ's September policy decision — was released today; private-sector consensus (10-institution average) pointed to a third consecutive quarterly expansion near +2.1% annualized, with private consumption as the primary driver and a mild drag from softer exports. **Bond rout puts the honebuto's funding math at risk (#82, Aug 19, 2026):** The 10-year JGB yield pushed toward 2.95–3% this week, a level last seen in 1996 and the exact threshold the government used as its budget assumption, with an early-August 10-year auction drawing the weakest demand in a year. A sustained move above 3% would push debt-servicing costs past the ¥31tn ($195bn) currently budgeted, squeezing room for the honebuto's own ¥370tn pledge. The immediate flashpoint is Takaichi's plan to cut the consumption tax on food to 1% for two years without an identified offsetting revenue source, even as she maintains overall JGB issuance will stay unchanged — a combination bond investors are pricing skeptically given debt already above 200% of GDP, while LDP conservatives simultaneously press her to curb spending. **IP Strategy Headquarters: draft AI training-data disclosure code (#82, Aug 18, 2026):** A separate Cabinet Office body, the Intellectual Property Strategy Headquarters (知的財産戦略本部), unveiled a draft 'comply or explain' principles code for generative-AI (生成AI, seisei AI) developers, built on the AI-related technology law enacted May 2025. Three principles: public disclosure of models used, training data, and collection methods (sensitive data exempted); domain-specific disclosure to rights holders alleging infringement; and a duty to respond to user requests about possible copyright infringement. The code is non-binding — businesses may comply or publicly explain why they do not — a soft-law complement to Japan's copyright statute rather than new hard regulation. **Code formally adopted (#89, Aug 25, 2026):** The government adopted the revised 'Principle-Code for Protection of Intellectual Property and Transparency for the Appropriate Use of Generative AI' — moving from the Aug 18 draft to a Cabinet-level adoption after a Dec 2025–Jan 2026 public consultation. The adopted code applies to generative-AI developers and providers whose systems are offered in Japan or to Japanese nationals, including foreign firms, and sets concrete compliance expectations: respecting paywalls and robots.txt, avoiding pirate sites, retaining training logs, taking technical measures against infringing outputs, and establishing rights-holder contact points. As a comply-or-explain framework it carries no statutory penalty, but it gives Japanese rights holders and regulators a reference standard to cite in disputes with both domestic and foreign AI developers — a distinct escalation from the draft-stage coverage in that it is now the operative document companies will be measured against. **Execution risk surfaces in Kitakami (#96, Sept 1-2, 2026):** Bloomberg and the Japan Times profiled Kitakami, a city of roughly 90,000 in Iwate Prefecture 500km north of Tokyo, as a test case for whether the honebuto's ¥101.6tn AI-and-chip allocation (part of the broader ¥370tn/¥640bn USD pledge) translates into durable regional growth. Kioxia's Kitakami plant (see Kioxia entity, Fab3 ¥1tn expansion) has brought new tech workers and infrastructure spending to the area, but reporting found the boost concentrated narrowly around the factory gates — limited local-supply-chain formation, housing and services still shaped more by decades of rural depopulation than by the AI-investment wave, and skepticism among residents about whether the ¥370tn pledge's benefits will broaden beyond direct plant employment. It's a ground-level complement to the Cabinet Office's own Aug 7 GDP-forecast downgrade: the growth strategy's macro numbers depend on regional multiplier effects that, one year in, are not yet visibly showing up outside a handful of factory towns.

tags.l: Kitakami case study: narrow multiplier so far (Sep 1-2)

entities.name: Sakana AI
entities.desc: Japan's most internationally prominent AI research lab, founded by two of the most credentialed AI researchers in the world (David Ha + Llion Jones, Transformer co-inventor). **Evolutionary model merging:** Sakana AI's primary research direction is 'AI for AI' — using evolutionary algorithms and model merging to automatically compose or improve existing foundation models without gradient descent retraining, offering potentially 10x+ compute reduction versus training from scratch. **Sovereignty through post-training:** Rather than compete on frontier pretraining compute, Sakana fine-tunes and orchestrates other labs' open-weight models (Moonshot AI's Kimi, Google's Gemma) into Japan-specific products — its free Sakana Translate service, upgraded Aug 21 to the new-generation Namazu model, beat rival translation services in head-to-head evaluation on culturally specific Japanese text. **AI Scientist (2024):** Published a paper on an AI system that autonomously generates, runs, and writes up machine learning research experiments — widely cited as the first plausible automated AI research system. **Funding trajectory:** The $430M raise at $1B+ valuation (2024) makes it the largest single venture round for a Japan-based AI startup in history. **Comprehensive partnership with Sumitomo Corp and SCSK (#104, Sept 10, 2026):** Sakana AI, trading house Sumitomo Corporation, and IT services firm SCSK announced a comprehensive business partnership to accelerate enterprise AI deployment in Japan, combining Sakana's research and its Japan-developed orchestration model with Sumitomo's business-development reach and SCSK's systems-integration capability. Initial work targets finance and manufacturing use cases, with cybersecurity and overseas expansion flagged as follow-on areas — a distinct commercialization channel from Sakana's existing SDF command-layer and translation-product work, moving the lab further from pure research toward enterprise deployment via established corporate distribution partners rather than building its own sales organization. **Fugu Ultra v2 ships with Claude Fable 5/5.1 and GPT-6 Astra excluded from its pool (#106, Sept 11, 2026):** Sakana shipped a refreshed version of its multi-agent orchestration model, Fugu Ultra v2, alongside a cheaper sibling, Fugu Max. The pool composition change is the story: Sakana explicitly removed three of the strongest models now shipping (Claude Fable 5, Fable 5.1, GPT-6 Astra) from the coordinator's available pool and still claims best-or-joint-best placement on 5 of 8 benchmarks, including a 21-point vendor-reported gap over Claude Opus 5 on visual reasoning (Chartography). All figures are vendor-reported with no independent evaluation published and no per-task routing disclosed -- Sakana's FAQ states routing information is not exposed by design. Pricing is unchanged from the June launch ($5/$30 per 1M tokens for Ultra); the product remains unavailable in the EU/EEA pending GDPR compliance work. **Tops Nikkei/Kepple H1 2026 startup funding ranking as investor base narrows (#109, Sept 15-16, 2026):** Nikkei Asia reported Sakana ranked first in Japan's H1 2026 startup funding league table compiled with data provider Kepple Group, as Japanese venture investors grew more selective — concentrating capital on a smaller number of companies with track records rather than spreading bets broadly. Japanese startups raised a combined ¥377.9bn in H1 2026, up 12% year-on-year, with research-intensive companies (deep tech, AI, robotics) accounting for roughly 44% (¥167.5bn) of that total — the clearest sign yet that the 'flight to quality' dynamic already visible in Sakana's own late-2025 Series B (at a ¥400bn/$2.65bn valuation) has become a market-wide pattern rather than a company-specific story. Self-driving software startup Turing ranked among the other top winners. **Launches Frontier Intelligence Group, a formal bet against pure Transformer scaling (#118, Sept 18, 2026):** Sakana AI stood up an internal research collective, the Frontier Intelligence Group (FIG), organized around five speculative projects that share one premise -- that the Transformer architecture anchoring AI progress since 2017 may not be the only path worth funding. The projects span biologically inspired "Continuous Thought Machines," a backpropagation-free training method (Augmented Lagrangian Predictive Coding, or PC-ALM) that trains 1,000-layer networks with only local layer-by-layer updates and lands within about two points of standard backprop accuracy on deep test networks, a sparse-Transformer collaboration with Nvidia aimed at cutting the memory and energy cost of running billion-parameter models, an evolutionary image-generation experiment, and a self-organizing physical-hardware project. CTO Llion Jones -- a co-author of the original 2017 Transformer paper -- said the architecture's own success "has stifled the kind of research freedom that allowed for its very inception." Only the Nvidia sparse-Transformer work has an obvious near-term commercial path; the rest remain unproven outside small image-classification benchmarks. The more useful read for positioning is that FIG is insurance and recruiting leverage rather than a product roadmap -- a hedge against transformer-scaling fatigue and a pitch to researchers who want to work outside the current scaling-law consensus, distinct from Sakana's existing orchestration/fine-tuning business (Fugu) and its Sept 10-16 funding and partnership news already tracked above.

The model: member companies pool capital for teleoperation rigs that cost $50,000-150,000 each — prohibitive for any single mid-market manufacturer — and in exchange all resulting training data becomes shared IP across the consortium, distinct from both Japan's government-backed FRONTia/Noetra program (open-weights foundation models) and single-company proprietary data factories like Samsung's Gumi facility. A parallel 'data collection kit' service lets outside companies contribute their own facility data in exchange for preferential access to J-HRTI's broader dataset. Target: real-world humanoid deployment in manufacturing/logistics by end of Japan's FY2026 (March 2027), with expansion to 10 data-collection sites nationwide targeted for 2027.

tags.l: Kanto Data Factory opened Chiba, 35 humanoids (Aug 26)
Shared-IP model: cost pooled, data commons to members

entities.name: ASML Japan
entities.desc: The Dutch EUV-lithography monopolist's Japan subsidiary — a single-vendor chokepoint for every leading-edge logic fab in the country, and a bellwether for how seriously equipment suppliers are underwriting Japan's chip revival. **40% workforce expansion announced (#98, Sept 3-4, 2026):** ASML Japan President Shojiro Fujiwara told a Thursday press conference the company will grow its domestic headcount from roughly 500 to about 700 by 2030 to keep pace with advanced chip production in the country. The Hokkaido office, opened in 2024 specifically to support Rapidus's Chitose fab, has already grown its engineering team from 24 to 50; Kumamoto is a second likely beneficiary as TSMC builds its second JASM fab there, and the expansion follows TSMC's Aug 11 definitive agreement with Sony Group to form a dedicated image-sensor joint venture in the same prefecture. ASML's Japan sales reached roughly $1.4bn in 2025, with Rapidus, TSMC, and Micron's Hiroshima facility among its named domestic customers — meaning the hiring plan is best read as ASML pre-positioning field-service and applications-engineering capacity ahead of Rapidus's 2027 2nm ramp and TSMC's Kumamoto Fab 2, rather than a response to demand that has already materialized.

tags.l: Kumamoto (TSMC 2nd fab) staff growth likely next

entities.bio: ASML Japan is the Japan subsidiary of ASML Holding N.V. (founded 1984, Veldhoven, Netherlands; listed Euronext Amsterdam and Nasdaq as ASML), the world's sole supplier of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography systems required for sub-7nm logic chip production. Opened a dedicated Hokkaido support office in 2024 to service Rapidus's Chitose fab; also supplies TSMC's JASM Kumamoto fabs and Micron's Hiroshima facility.

entities.name: Turing
entities.desc: Tokyo-based end-to-end autonomous-driving software startup, one of Japan's most-funded AI startups and a named winner alongside Sakana AI in Nikkei/Kepple's H1 2026 startup-funding ranking. **Business model:** Turing does not build vehicles — it develops deep-learning-based autonomous driving software (trained on real-world driving data rather than hand-coded rules) that carmakers and robotaxi operators could license, positioning it as a software-layer bet on Japan's auto industry rather than a hardware challenger. **Capital base:** Raised roughly ¥27.9bn in an extended Series A (completed by July 2026), with equity backers including AMD Ventures, Mitsubishi Corporation, MUFG Bank, Super Micro Computer, Tokyo Electron Device, and Denso — giving it deep ties across Japan's auto and chip-equipment supply chains. Uses AMD GPUs for cost competitiveness against Nvidia-based rivals. **Ambition and competitive set:** CEO Issei Yamamoto has outlined plans for a US office focused on driving-data collection and a potential public listing within five years at a valuation near $10bn — an explicit attempt to compete data-for-data with Tesla, Waymo, and Chinese autonomy players. Domestically, Turing faces a competing Tokyo robotaxi pilot from Nissan, UK's Wayve, and Uber targeted for later in 2026, making Turing's H1 2026 fundraising strength a signal of investor conviction in Japan's home-grown alternative to that coalition.

tags.l: Named top-tier H1 2026 funding winner alongside Sakana (Sept 15-16)

entities.bio: Founded 2021, Tokyo, by CEO Issei Yamamoto. Private; backed by Denso, MUFG Bank, AMD Ventures, Mitsubishi Corporation, Super Micro Computer, and Tokyo Electron Device. Develops end-to-end deep-learning autonomous driving software for driver-assistance and robotaxi applications, targeting Japan and the US.

entities.name: Samsung Electronics (Japan Packaging)
entities.zh: サムスン電子（日本パッケージング）
entities.desc: South Korea's Samsung Electronics is deepening its footprint in Japan's back-end (advanced packaging) supply chain rather than front-end fabrication, betting that Japan's strength in packaging materials — not logic nodes — is the next axis of AI-chip competition. **Advanced Package Lab (APL) opens in Yokohama (#109, Sept 8, 2026):** Samsung held an opening ceremony for its APL in the Minato Mirai district — a ~6,600 sqm facility with a clean room for evaluating back-end materials and prototyping under real production conditions. Total investment is ¥40bn ($277M), of which Japan's METI is funding ¥22.5bn (over half), plus a ¥2.5bn subsidy from the City of Yokohama. Ninety-five South Korean and Japanese researchers will work on packaging technology for HBM (High Bandwidth Memory) and GPU integration — the back-end steps that connect multiple chips together and are emerging as a new competitive axis as front-end circuit miniaturization approaches physical limits. **Supply-chain significance:** Samsung already works with 50+ Japanese companies on AI-chip back-end processes; Japan holds outsized share in packaging materials (Sumitomo Bakelite ~40% of global encapsulation materials; Resonac and Mitsubishi Gas Chemical lead in substrate materials). Fifteen major Japanese chip firms, including Tokyo Electron and Ibiden, attended the opening — a direct read-through for TEL's equipment-and-materials revenue base distinct from its TSMC/JASM exposure. The Yokohama base lets Samsung evaluate and prototype with Japanese materials locally before porting only validated technologies to Korean mass-production lines, and is explicitly framed as competing with TSMC (#1 in advanced packaging) and SK Hynix (HBM leader) by tightening Samsung's own back-end supply chain.

tags.l: APL opens Yokohama, ¥40bn total, METI funds >half (Sept 8)

entities.bio: Samsung Electronics (founded 1969, Suwon, South Korea; listed Korea Exchange 005930) is the world's largest memory-chip maker. This entry tracks its Japan-based advanced-packaging R&D operations, distinct from its Korean fabs — a strategic bet on Japanese back-end materials expertise (encapsulation, substrates) to strengthen its position in AI-chip packaging against TSMC and SK Hynix.

entities.name: GlobalFoundries
entities.zh: グローバルファウンドリーズ
entities.bio: US-headquartered contract chipmaker (foundry) spun off from AMD's manufacturing operations in 2009, listed on Nasdaq since 2021. Focuses on specialty and logic semiconductor manufacturing rather than leading-edge process nodes.
entities.desc: Reportedly in line to operate a proposed $12.85bn-$19bn (¥2-3tn) logic-chip fab in the US, to be funded as part of Japan's $550bn tariff-deal investment package with Washington -- the first tariff-related Japanese investment to target chip manufacturing rather than power projects. Working-level Japan-US talks were held Sept 14-15, 2026; officials are still negotiating how the investment would be recouped.

entities.name: THK Corporation
entities.bio: Founded 1971, Tokyo. Global leader in linear motion (LM) guide systems for machine tools and robotics. Listed TSE (6481). Core business supplies precision motion components used across the robotics and factory-automation industry.
entities.desc: Demonstrated a teleoperated robot at Tokyo's Physical AI Summit (Sept 16, 2026) that picks up bottles, bags and boxes and can hammer a nail into wood using articulated arms and grippers, showcasing precision manipulation built on THK's own linear-motion component expertise.

entities.name: ugo
entities.bio: Japanese robotics venture developing semi-humanoid robots for remote operation and physical-AI data collection. Core product: the ugo Nova platform.
entities.desc: Demonstrated its ugo Nova semi-humanoid performing a teleoperated drilling task at Tokyo's Physical AI Summit (Sept 16, 2026). ugo Nova uses two seven-axis arms plus additional head and waist joints, and is designed to collect real-world manipulation data that feeds back into training ugo's own physical-AI models — a hardware-first approach to building physical AI capability.

tags.l: Data-collection strategy for physical AI training

entities.name: Fujifilm
entities.bio: Founded 1934, Tokyo. Diversified imaging, materials, and healthcare conglomerate. Listed TSE (4901). Semiconductor-materials business supplies process chemicals and high-purity materials to global chipmakers.
entities.desc: Announced a ₹800 crore ($83M) investment in a new semiconductor-materials plant in India (Semicon India 2026, Sept 19), targeting front-end process chemicals in Phase 1 (construction FY2026, production FY2028) and surface-conditioning/high-purity chemicals in Phase 2. Signed an MoU with Tata Electronics to supply materials for Tata's Dholera, Gujarat fab.

entities.name: Sumitomo Chemical
entities.bio: Founded 1913, Tokyo. Major Japanese chemicals conglomerate spanning petrochemicals, materials, and semiconductor-grade chemicals. Listed TSE (4005).
entities.desc: Signed an MoU with Tata Electronics (Sept 2026) to supply semiconductor materials — photoresists and high-purity chemicals including hydrogen peroxide, isopropyl alcohol, ammonia water, and sulfuric acid — for Tata's upcoming Dholera, Gujarat fab, and will explore local manufacturing of these materials in India.

entities.name: Hirata Corporation
entities.bio: Founded 1951, Kumamoto. Japanese automation and material-handling equipment maker serving semiconductor, display, and automotive manufacturing. Listed TSE (6258).
entities.desc: Bringing its semiconductor automation and material-handling portfolio into India through subsidiary ATS India (announced Sept 2026) — Equipment Front End Modules (EFEM), FOPLP load ports, panel-handling robots, and high-performance wafer-handling robots used in fabrication and advanced packaging.

entities.name: Preferred Computing Infrastructure (PFCI)
entities.zh: プリファードコンピューティングインフラストラクチャー
entities.bio: Founded 2025 in Tokyo as a Preferred Networks (PFN) Group company. Builds and operates high-efficiency AI computing infrastructure powered primarily by PFN's MN-Core series accelerators, delivered as the Preferred Computing Platform (PFCP) AI cloud service.
entities.desc: PFN's dedicated AI-cloud vehicle, standing up compute infrastructure around PFN's proprietary MN-Core chips rather than third-party GPUs. **MN-Core 2 for Matlantis (#116, Sept 18, 2026):** PFCI and PFN announced PFCP will offer MN-Core 2 as a selectable compute resource for Matlantis, PFN's commercial materials-discovery simulator — PFCI's first prominent public role in bringing an in-house PFN Group product to an external paying customer base via MN-Core-powered cloud compute.

tags.l: MN-Core 2 for Matlantis via PFCP cloud platform (Sept 18)

entities.name: CADDi
entities.bio: Founded in 2017 by Yusaku Kato and Kenta Suenaga, CADDi builds AI software that reads manufacturers' engineering drawings and structures the data locked inside them. Its original product, CADDi Drawer (2022), let engineers search archived part designs by shape or specification rather than by filename; the platform has since broadened into what the company calls an AI data platform for manufacturing, pulling together CAD files, ERP records, and other factory-floor data sources. Backed by Atomico, Globis Capital Partners, and Japan Post Asset Management prior to its Series D.
entities.desc: **$114mn Series D at $1.2bn valuation, unicorn status (#117, Sept 24, 2026):** CADDi raised ¥17.7bn ($114mn) on Sept 16, lifting its valuation to ¥182bn ($1.2bn) and crossing into unicorn territory. New investors Moore Strategic Ventures, Coreline Ventures, Salesforce Ventures, and Toyota's Woven Capital joined returning backers Atomico, Globis Capital Partners, and Japan Post Asset Management, taking total funding to $234mn. Proceeds are earmarked for proprietary AI development and North American expansion, where manufacturers face the same drawing-search problem CADDi solved domestically but with far less existing AI tooling built for factory-floor use.

tags.l: Toyota's Woven Capital joins as new investor

entities.name: Panasonic Energy
entities.zh: パナソニックエナジー
entities.bio: Panasonic Energy is the battery subsidiary of Panasonic Holdings, a longtime lithium-ion cell supplier to Tesla and other automakers. The unit has been expanding beyond automotive cells into data-center and next-generation battery chemistries as EV demand growth has slowed relative to earlier forecasts.
entities.desc: **Opens 500-person battery R&D hub, targets 2x development efficiency by FY2031 (#117, Sept 24, 2026):** Panasonic Energy opened Energy Innovation Square in Kadoma, Osaka on Sept 16 -- a lithium-ion battery R&D facility staffed by roughly 500 researchers covering materials development, cell design, and prototyping under one roof. Combined with the adjacent Suminoe production-development site (about 800 staff total), it forms one of Japan's largest dedicated battery-development clusters. Panasonic named automotive and data-center batteries as its immediate priority, with drones, robotaxis, and humanoid robots flagged as future demand categories rather than markets it is building capacity against today.

tags.l: Energy Innovation Square opens in Kadoma, Osaka (Sept 16)
Robotics/robotaxi batteries named as future, not current, priority

entities.name: EdgeCortix
entities.zh: エッジコーティックス
entities.bio: Founded 2019 in Tokyo by Sakyasingha Dasgupta, a former AI researcher, EdgeCortix designs energy-efficient AI accelerators for edge and robotics workloads. Its products include the SAKURA-II edge AI chip, the runtime-reconfigurable DNA-X accelerator architecture and the MERA software stack. Privately held.
entities.desc: **RAIDEN physical-AI chiplet platform (#120, Sept 24, 2026):** Launched a scalable chiplet family; the four-die RAIDEN-X4 delivers up to 3.36 PFLOPS FP4, 256 GB memory and 1.54 TB/s die-to-die bandwidth (~1.6x Jetson AGX Thor per MONOist). Kawasaki Heavy Industries selected it for aerospace and defense products and Unigen is building servers. Sampling early 2027, volume 2H 2027; foundry, node and pricing undisclosed.

entities.name: Nippon Life Insurance
entities.bio: Japan's largest life insurer, founded 1889 in Osaka as a mutual company. One of the largest institutional holders of JGBs and foreign bonds, and an expanding lender to infrastructure and AI data center projects.
entities.desc: **AI data center lender under FSA review (#120, Sept 25, 2026):** About ¥1 trillion of AI infrastructure loans outstanding as of March 2026, with a ¥2 trillion target by 2035 at project-finance spreads above 2 points; lending mainly to US hyperscaler projects including Amazon. Plans a dedicated screening team next year as the FSA steps up scrutiny.

tags.l: FSA review of US data center loans

entities.name: Mitsubishi Chemical Group
entities.zh: 三菱ケミカルグループ
entities.bio: Japan's largest chemical group, formed through the 2017 merger of Mitsubishi Chemical, Mitsubishi Plastics and Mitsubishi Rayon under the Mitsubishi Chemical Holdings umbrella (renamed Mitsubishi Chemical Group in 2022), headquartered in Tokyo. Its semiconductor exposure runs through specialty materials, including gallium nitride (GaN) single-crystal substrates produced at its Tsukuba site in Ibaraki. Listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange Prime market.
entities.desc: **6-inch GaN substrates for power chips (#121, Sept 24, 2026):** Mitsubishi Chemical will ship 6-inch gallium nitride substrate samples for power semiconductors to customers by March 2027, targeting AI data center power conversion and EV/autonomous drivetrains. 4-inch substrates are in mass production at Tsukuba (mainly for projector lasers) and under customer evaluation for power devices; a GaN single-crystal pilot line with Japan Steel Works in Muroran, Hokkaido is preparing 6-inch samples, and 8-inch is in development. CTO Masaru Utsunomiya said late entrants struggle once the supply window closes; the company is weighing location and timing for large-diameter capacity.

tags.l: Pilot line with Japan Steel Works, Muroran
No capex or device partner announced yet

entities.name: Sakai Chemical Industry
entities.bio: Founded 1918 in Sakai, Osaka, from a zinc oxide business whose early products included white face powder (oshiroi) used in traditional makeup. Makes titanium dioxide, zinc and barium compounds, cosmetic and pharmaceutical materials, and electronic materials. Listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange Prime market.
entities.desc: One of a handful of merchant suppliers of hydrothermally synthesized barium titanate (チタン酸バリウム), the fine dielectric powder stacked inside multilayer ceramic capacitors (MLCCs); Murata makes much of its own powder in-house. **AI-server capacitor bottleneck (#122, Bloomberg Sept 27 / Japan Times Sept 28, 2026):** Bloomberg reported that capacity for its capacitor raw materials is filling quickly as AI servers, which carry far more MLCCs per rack than conventional servers, pull demand upstream. Electronic materials are a minority of group sales next to titanium dioxide, cosmetic and pharmaceutical materials, so pricing and new capacity decide how much of the AI demand reaches earnings. **Peer expansion:** Nippon Chemical Industrial said Aug 18, 2026 it will raise barium titanate capacity about 1.5x in FY2027 for AI-server MLCCs; on Sept 28 Sakai announced its exit from pharmacopoeia-grade barium sulfate.

tags.l: Peer Nippon Chemical adding 1.5x capacity FY2027
Electronic materials a minority of sales

entities.name: SAIMEMORY
entities.bio: Established December 2024 and launched in June 2025 as a SoftBank subsidiary, with the University of Tokyo as a research partner; CEO Hideya Yamaguchi. Develops Z-Angle Memory (ZAM), a stacked DRAM for AI built on Intel's Next Generation DRAM Bonding work under a partnership formalized in February 2026. Series A funding included SoftBank, Fujitsu, the Development Bank of Japan and RIKEN; the program also receives NEDO support.
entities.desc: SoftBank's attempt to put Japan back into advanced DRAM with an alternative to HBM. **Shinko Electric packaging deal (#123, Sept 28, 2026):** basic agreement with Shinko Electric Industries to co-develop the packaging, assembly and manufacturing processes for ZAM, which stands DRAM dies upright side by side (versus HBM's flat stack, heat-limited at about 20 layers) and links them with magnetically coupled wireless I/O. Targets: prototypes in FY2027, practical use in FY2029. **VLSI Symposium demo with Intel (#15, June 2026):** ZAM-based HB3DM design claimed roughly 40% lower power than conventional HBM; up to 512GB per chip targeted.

tags.l: Unproven at volume; HBM incumbents moving fast

entities.name: Shinko Electric Industries
entities.bio: Founded 1946 in Nagano. Maker of flip-chip package substrates, lead frames and electrostatic chucks for high-end processors and chipmaking equipment. Formerly a listed Fujitsu subsidiary; taken private in 2025 by a consortium led by the state-backed Japan Investment Corporation with Dai Nippon Printing and Mitsui Chemicals.
entities.desc: One of Japan's key advanced-packaging substrate suppliers for AI processors. **Buys JDI's Mobara plant for FC-BGA expansion (#126, Sept 30, 2026):** agreed to acquire Japan Display's idle 373,000 m² Mobara LCD plant in Chiba as a new core plant for flip-chip (FC-BGA) substrates used in AI accelerators and data center chips; the western ~233,000 m² goes to supplier FICT for circuit boards. Transfer end-March 2027, production from FY2028; price undisclosed, JDI books a ¥51.4B gain. Shinko said Nagano sites lack room for the larger, higher-layer substrates AI chips need. **ZAM packaging partner for SAIMEMORY (#123, Sept 28, 2026):** basic agreement to develop packaging and high-density assembly for SoftBank-backed SAIMEMORY's Z-Angle Memory, targeting practical use in FY2029.

tags.l: Buys JDI Mobara plant for FC-BGA (Sept 30)
New capacity arrives after current crunch

entities.name: TDK Corporation
entities.bio: Founded in 1935 in Tokyo by Kenzo Saito to commercialize ferrite, a magnetic material invented at Tokyo Institute of Technology. Now a diversified electronic-components maker spanning multilayer ceramic capacitors, inductors, sensors, and lithium-ion battery cells for phones and devices. Listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange Prime market.
entities.desc: One of Japan's four large passive-component makers, with a battery business that gives it exposure to consumer devices and power storage. **MOU with Taiyo Yuden on AI-grade components (#124, Sept 29, 2026):** TDK and Taiyo Yuden signed a memorandum of understanding to explore joint development of high-capacitance MLCCs and inductors for AI data centers, servers and physical AI, plus cooperation in manufacturing and procurement, and will consider a capital alliance. The partners may seek joint METI approval under the Economic Security Promotion Act. TDK shares rose about 1.3-2.5% on Sept 30 while Murata fell 2.7%.

tags.l: AI server MLCC and inductor demand
No terms or timeline; integration risk

entities.name: Taiyo Yuden
entities.bio: Founded in 1950 in Tokyo by Kenji Sato as a maker of ceramic capacitors. Specializes in multilayer ceramic capacitors, inductors and high-frequency modules for smartphones, autos and servers. Listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange Prime market.
entities.desc: A pure-play passive-component maker whose earnings track MLCC pricing and the AI server build. **MOU with TDK on AI-grade components (#124, Sept 29, 2026):** agreed with TDK to explore joint development of high-capacitance, high-reliability MLCCs and inductors for AI data centers and physical AI, cooperation in manufacturing and procurement, and a possible capital alliance. Shares rose about 2.8-3.8% on Sept 30. The combination would pair the third- and fourth-largest MLCC makers against Murata, Samsung Electro-Mechanics and fast-growing Chinese suppliers.

tags.l: MLCC supply tight on AI servers

entities.name: JERA
entities.bio: Founded 2015 in Tokyo as a 50-50 joint venture of TEPCO (Tokyo Electric Power) and Chubu Electric Power, which merged their fuel procurement and thermal generation into it. Japan's largest power generator, producing roughly a third of the country's electricity, mostly from LNG-fired plants. Unlisted; exposure runs through its two listed parents.
entities.desc: **Power-plant AI data center model (#126, Oct 1, 2026):** signed an MOU with Dell Technologies and UK developer RHAELM to build a 400 MW, $15B+ AI data center beside its gas-fired Chiba thermal plant, with Apollo financing; JERA supplies land and 400 MW for 15-25 years, RHAELM builds and operates, Dell provides rack-scale AI servers. First operations 2028, full capacity 2029. The partners target several gigawatts at other JERA plants in the 2030s (FT: ~$140B full rollout). On-site power avoids grid-connection queues around Tokyo.

tags.l: Multi-GW plan across JERA plants in 2030s
No tenant named; LNG cost exposure

entities.name: Japan Display Inc. (JDI)
entities.zh: ジャパンディスプレイ
entities.bio: Formed in 2012 in Tokyo by merging the small and mid-size LCD units of Sony, Toshiba and Hitachi with backing from the state-backed Innovation Network Corporation of Japan. Maker of LCD and OLED panels for phones, cars and wearables. Listed on the TSE Prime market since 2014; later rescued by Ichigo Asset Management.
entities.desc: **Sells Mobara plant to Shinko Electric (#126, Sept 30, 2026):** agreed to sell its idle Mobara (Chiba) LCD plant, shut in November 2025, to Shinko Electric for advanced AI-chip substrates; transfer end-March 2027, with a ¥51.4B extraordinary gain in FY to March 2027. Micron had reportedly studied the site and JDI had floated a 100 MW data center there. **Restructuring:** ¥78.2B operating loss in FY to March 2025; sold Tottori plant March 2026 and is consolidating at Ishikawa. Its idle fabs are becoming supply for Japan's chip back-end and AI infrastructure buildout.

tags.l: Idle LCD fabs repurposed for AI chips

entities.name: ELYZA
entities.bio: Founded 2018 in Tokyo by alumni of Professor Yutaka Matsuo's lab at the University of Tokyo; CEO Yuya Soneoka. Builds Japanese-language LLMs and enterprise generative-AI products. KDDI took a controlling stake in 2024 and consolidates it as a subsidiary.
entities.desc: **Reasoning models on Japan's public base model (#128, Oct 2, 2026):** Released ELYZA-Thinking-1.0 in 33B dense and 32B-A3B mixture-of-experts versions under Apache 2.0, post-trained on NII's LLM-jp-4 with Japanese-translated math and code, several million synthetic reasoning examples (about half in Japanese) and reinforcement learning on verifiable tasks. The 33B model averages 61.7 on ELYZA's 20-benchmark suite, above NII's own LLM-jp-4.1 thinking model (60.6) and Qwen3-32B (58.1), below Qwen3.5-27B (68.2) and Gemma 4 31B (70.5). **ELYZA RSI Research:** A new unit for recursive self-improvement; ELYZA says agents handled most of the training and evaluation, with 1-2 person-days of human work per model, and describes this as groundwork rather than RSI itself. It also walked back an English 'fully domestic' claim. **Earlier:** Its Llama-based Japanese models claimed GPT-4-level Japanese scores in 2024, the result that preceded KDDI's investment.

tags.l: ELYZA RSI Research: agent-run model development

entities.name: National Institute of Informatics (NII)
entities.desc: Inter-university research institute in Tokyo that runs the LLM-jp project and its Research and Development Center for Large Language Models, Japan's main public effort to pre-train open LLMs from scratch. **LLM-jp-4.1 (#128, Sept 28, 2026):** Released 8B, 33B and 32B-A3B models with tool calling and stronger STEM results, trained on 11.7 trillion tokens, Apache 2.0, with SFT and DPO data published alongside. The 33B thinking model scored 7.76 on Japanese MT-Bench versus 7.29 for GPT-4o. **Downstream use:** KDDI's ELYZA built its ELYZA-Thinking-1.0 reasoning models on LLM-jp-4 within days, the first large commercial adoption of the public base model.

entities.name: Air Liquide Japan
entities.bio: Japanese arm of Paris-based industrial gas group Air Liquide (founded 1902), active in Japan's electronics sector for more than 40 years. Runs about 78 facilities in Japan and an advanced materials center in Tsukuba. Competes with Nippon Sanso Holdings (TSE: 4091) for on-site gas supply to chip fabs.
entities.desc: **€170M+ for a Kyushu logic fab (#128, Sept 30, 2026):** Will build, own and operate several ultra-high-purity gas units (nitrogen, oxygen, argon, hydrogen) plus large backup storage for an unnamed leading chipmaker's logic expansion in southern Japan, under a long-term supply contract. The profile matches TSMC JASM's 3nm second fab in Kumamoto. **€200M for Hiroshima (Apr 16, 2026):** Two units supplying ultra-pure nitrogen, oxygen and argon to a major chipmaker in Hiroshima, starting by end-2028. Together the two awards put about €370M of on-site gas capacity behind Japan's AI-chip buildout this year.

entities.name: Rohm
entities.bio: Founded in 1958 in Kyoto by Kenichiro Sato as a resistor maker (Toyo Denshi Kogyo) and renamed Rohm in 1981. Today a Kyoto-based maker of power and analog chips, with silicon carbide (SiC) as its growth bet after the 2009 acquisition of Germany's SiCrystal. Listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
entities.desc: **Power-chip merger talks stall (#130, Sept 30-Oct 2, 2026):** Rohm, Toshiba's device unit and Mitsubishi Electric signed a basic agreement on March 27, 2026 to integrate their power-semiconductor businesses, most likely under a holding company. Jiji reported on Sept 30 that the summer target has slipped because the three cannot agree on equity ratios, the scope of carved-out businesses and who leads; the new goal is the November interim results, with March 2027 as a fallback, and Chinese antitrust clearance is required. Combined, the group would rank second globally behind Infineon. METI minister Akazawa said on Oct 2 he would back domestic realignment. **Denso bid withdrawn (Apr 28, 2026):** Denso dropped its proposal to take a stake in Rohm after failing to secure board support, which cleared the way for the three-way talks. **SiC overhang:** Rohm's heavy SiC capex has met weak EV demand, the main reason it needs scale partners.

tags.l: 3-way power-chip merger talks slip to Nov or Mar 2027

entities.name: Goodman Group
entities.zh: グッドマン・グループ
entities.bio: Founded 1989 in Sydney by Greg Goodman as an industrial property developer; listed on the ASX and now Australia's largest property company by market value. It develops and manages logistics and industrial estates across Asia-Pacific, Europe and the Americas and has turned much of its development pipeline toward powered data center sites. Operates in Japan through Goodman Japan, a long-standing logistics warehouse developer around Greater Tokyo and Osaka.
entities.desc: **Tsukuba backlash (#131, Oct 7, 2026):** Goodman's planned 1 GW, roughly ¥3 trillion ($20bn) data center campus on a 45-hectare site in Tsukuba's Oho district, Ibaraki, one of the largest foreign-backed digital infrastructure projects in Japan, faces organised local opposition. The first 50 MW phase began construction earlier in 2026 next to housing, a hospital and a nursing home. Residents say 2023 filings described a logistics warehouse; about 800 have signed for a public town hall and threaten protests, while Goodman's only sessions so far were invitation-only dinners in August. Goodman says it exceeds legal requirements and will hold an information meeting after consulting the city. The dispute follows Goodman's withdrawal of a similar Sydney project after local resistance, and tests the Japan Data Center Council's May guidelines on community consultation.

entities.name: Anthropic
entities.bio: Founded 2021 in San Francisco by Dario Amodei, Daniela Amodei and other former OpenAI researchers. Develops the Claude family of large language models. Privately held; major investors include Amazon and Google.
entities.desc: **Nippan confirms bulk book sales to Anthropic (#132, Oct 6-7, 2026):** Nippan Group Holdings (日販グループホールディングス), one of Japan's two dominant book wholesalers, told the Japan Book Publishers Association that a group company sold large volumes of books to Anthropic between December 2024 and December 2025, while saying it did not know they were for AI training. The sales surfaced through documents in a US authors' class action against Anthropic that listed 'Nippan Japan' as a supplier. The publishers' association asked Nippan to stop supplying books for AI training. The episode lands six weeks after Tokyo adopted a voluntary 'Principles Code' (Aug 25) asking AI developers operating in Japan, including foreign ones, to disclose outlines of training data and collection methods.

tags.l: Copyright Act Art. 30-4 permits training use
